prompt: A surveyor pounds three stakes into a field and sights through them: all three land on one perfectly straight line. What single word describes points that lie on the same line?
hint: The prefix "co-" means "together," and the rest of the word names the figure they share.

hints.text: The prefix "co-" means "together," and the rest of the word names the figure they share.
Points on the same LINE are co-... something. Points on the same plane are coplanar.

explanation: Points that all lie on one line are called collinear.
The word breaks apart as "co-" (together) plus "linear" (line).
If the stakes had NOT lined up, they would be noncollinear — and any three noncollinear points determine exactly one plane.

alternativeExplanations.title: Sort the vocabulary
steps: Collinear = same line. Coplanar = same flat surface.
A surveyor sighting through stakes is checking the line, so the word is collinear.
